entries.title: Isaiah 32:1
segments:
In this and the three following chapters promises and threatenings are mingled together.  Mighty judgments are coming upon sinners in Zion, and upon her enemies without; but amid all these, Christ's kingdom shall advance to its final establishment over all the earth.  Though the immediate occasion of these prophecies may have been the invasion of Sennacherib, they cannot be restricted to that event.  They cover the whole history of the church. 
 
  A king; the Messiah.  The word applies to earthly rulers of the church, such as Hezekiah, only so far as they have Christ's spirit, and exercise their authority under him. 
 
  Princes; under the king. 
 
From the beginning to the end of time, Christ is to his church the source of life and strength and wisdom and holiness.  From him alone are her rulers replenished with grace, and enabled to administer her affairs "in judgment," for the glory of God and her edification.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:2
segments: A man; the king spoken of in the preceding verse.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:3
segments:
vv 3-8. 
 
  Shall not be dim--shall he stand; the general meaning is, that knowledge shall take the place of ignorance and men shall no longer "call evil good and good evil."

The rash--the stammerers; those who are rash and stammer in their judgment of spiritual things. 
 
  The churl; a man destitute alike of truth and mercy, as is plain from the prophet's description. 
 
vv 3-5. The religion of Christ, by purifying the affections of the heart, removes the great source of error, and enables men to judge correctly of moral principles and actions.  In this way the general prevalence of the gospel corrects public sentiment, and maintains it in a healthful condition.  But whenever irreligion prevails, perverse opinions and wicked practices go hand in hand.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:9
segments:
vv 9-12. 
 
  Rise up, ye women--the fruitful vine; a threatening against "the daughters of Zion" similiar to that in

. 
 
  The vintage shall fail; because of the invasion of the enemy. Compare

. 
 
  They shall lament for the teats; literally, "for the breasts," that is, the full breasts which have supplied nourishment to their infants. Food shall be wanting for mother and offspring. 
 
Luxury, idleness, and prodigality in females are heinous sins in the sight of God.  They exert a powerful influence to corrupt public morals, and thus bring upon nations and families those heavy judgments in which woman has so large a share of suffering.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:13
segments: Thorns and briers; because it is left desolate and untilled. Compare

. 
 
vv 13-18. The downward tendency of human nature mainfests itself in the church of Christ, as well as in the world.  But among his own people, God will not allow error and corruption to gain the victory.  In the midst of his judgments he will from time to time pour upon them his Spirit from on high, renovating their faith, and producing a new and abundant harvest of the fruits of righteousness.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:14
segments:
Forts and towers; literally, "Ophel and tower," that is, Ophel and its tower.  Ophel is a ridge extending south from the ancient temple area. 
 
  For ever; not absolutely, but through a long period of time, as the next verse shows.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:19
segments:
Coming down on the forest; or "in the fall of the forest."  "The forest" represents the pride and strength of the enemy.  Compare Isa 10.18-19,33-34. 
 
  The city; the city of the enemy--Nineveh, Babylon, and all like persecuting powers to the end of time. 
 
vv 19-20. The destruction of Satan's power, and the establishment of Christ's kingdom, are inseparably connected in God's plan, and shall be effected by the same instrumentalities.

entries.title: Isaiah 32:20
segments: Blessed are ye; that is, "my people."
The quiet and peaceful pursuit of agriculture is here a symbol for prosperity, temporal and spiritual.
